executable_actions.rationale: After the identity gate passes, execute a fresh exact-source replay and classify any pre-terminal termination before a hardware repair. The registry lacks a tool role that guarantees untruncated remote VCS causal provenance, so planned_tool.remote_vcs_termination_provenance is a required multi-agent capability implementation gap. It must collect raw runner/simulator context, the last HDL location/process/event when available, the final committed progress event, and active testbench observation processes without changing immutable artifacts or checker schemas.

executable_actions.rationale: When the static binding and fresh termination classification permit execution, rerun the required board-layer DAG with the exact wrapper and immutable semantic inputs. Require target-model expected outputs for the same stimulus/checkpoint, complete Transformer-block-only tensor coverage, unchanged numeric comparison, data order, liveness, AXI/DDR behavior, and executed DUT weight-consumption proof. This is the only path to replace the rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts and reconcile the active retry/barrier records.

observations: real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface failed before board functional execution because the simulation source-identity hash, Vivado-export compile authority, ordered-command authority references, and simulator executable authorization do not bind the current exact sample-project identity. This is a current board-integration verification-contract failure, not an RTL failure.

functional_sim=fail is dependency closure: case_vcs_functional_sim, the VCS evidence analyzer, and all downstream multilayer, AXI, DDR, deadlock, and semantic-evidence gates were not run. The missing board semantic-evidence report is therefore consequential and must not be repaired as an independent report-schema defect.

The current debug closure has no failed boundary, no representative failing transaction, no root-candidate module, and no lower-layer evidence contradiction. Certified leaf and connected-kernel evidence remains reusable. In particular, the connected kernel remains an elastic variable-latency token pipeline with certified boundary order and cross-token overlap; unequal stage durations are not a failure.

The prior hash-bound VCS SIGSEGV is retained as a failure lesson, but its diagnosis is historical-only after a live source-hash change. It cannot support a current hardware conclusion. A fresh replay must capture untruncated simulator/runner provenance, final committed progress, and active observation-process context.

sacg_memory_truth reports 15 active in-scope contamination barriers and six open in-scope retry requests, including retry_request.0143 and retry_request.0144 for the current case_axi_ddr_interface/functional_sim failure. Rejected Stage7 and Stage8 artifacts remain planning/debug evidence only until a newly checked Stage7 candidate is produced; there are no active in-scope backtrack requests.
The conditional design-team route returned no_split. It supplies no specialist override and does not replace the deterministic checker evidence.
proposed_actions: Rebuild only the current board simulation identity/authority binding from the exact user-supplied project and current Vivado exports, preserving all immutable functional and numeric artifacts; rerun case_axi_ddr_interface before attempting VCS.

Add the missing bounded simulator-termination provenance capability and execute a fresh exact-source VCS replay with current boundary/progress capture. Classify the termination before proposing any DUT or testbench semantic edit.

Only after a valid current replay is available, run the remaining Stage7 board DAG in dependency order, assemble semantic evidence, and update SACG retry/barrier state from checker-observed results. Any source repair after a real failure must target the earliest current board boundary; lower layers remain closed absent a named contradiction.
risks: A manifest-only repair can falsely appear to enable simulation while selecting a stale wrapper, a non-exported compile command, an unauthorized executable, or an inferred top module. The binding must be reconstructed from current exact sample-project and Vivado evidence, not guessed.

No board claim may be made without an immutable same-checkpoint/same-stimulus target-model inference result, resolved unchanged numeric comparison policy, semantic-testbench hash, complete Transformer-block tensor catalog, and executed proof that the DUT consumed every required bound Transformer-block weight. On-disk weights or manifests alone are insufficient.

The earlier SIGSEGV could be simulator/runner infrastructure, testbench observation activity, or deterministic HDL behavior. Editing RTL, VCD/report logic, goldens, tolerance, checkpoint, stimulus, or target reference before provenance classification would be speculative and could conceal the failure.

A prefetch/AXI or ingress/stage-0 progress symptom, including a missing output frontier, does not reopen the certified connected kernel. Revalidation of that kernel requires a fresh hash-bound trace with direct core start, ingress, egress, named causal-boundary evidence, and an explicit contradiction of its current certificate.

Backend synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime ABI, and board runtime remain blocked until every current board-layer gate passes with real-tool evidence and the active SACG retry/trust-barrier records are reconciled by the checked candidate.

First repair and recheck the current board integration/verification binding without altering immutable semantic inputs, then obtain fresh hash-bound VCS termination provenance and a current-layer trace before any RTL, lower-layer, backend, or board-runtime action.
